content:
There's a problem where Lake's git clone is too heavy and slow.
I've submitted a PR for lake that does a shallow clone, what do you think? Test passes, but I don't know detail about lake dependency resolving, it might cause some problem.

As a result, the size ends up about 20x smaller, and it's about 6x faster...

lean4#12513
https://github.com/SnO2WMaN/lean4-issue-10603/blob/main/results.md

Because of this, I just yesterday looked for something like a general central local cache for Git, and found the path-like variableGIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES. When there is a local central Mathlib clone at $MATHLIB, and GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES includes $MATHLIB/.git/objects, then the Lake clones become fast and small, too.

(Related, but not Git) Apart from that, I discovered the experimental Lake artifact cache. That makes builds of several Lake workspaces with the same dependencies small and fast. (For Mathlib, it seems like after a lake exe cache get, the Lake artifact cache has to be explicitly warmed with one more (quick) lake build. But then Lake builds of the same Mathlib revision as a dependency in other workspaces becomes small and fast, too.) The caching functionality apparently uses hard links. So the space savings can only be observed by df, not by du. And it may not save space on file systems without hard links, but I don't know.

I was annoyed by the disk usage and constant rebuilding especially in the context of playing with Verso (many Lake workspaces with the same dependencies). That now seems completely solved.
That was a bit off-topic, and possibly hijacking the thread. I think support for shallow cloning in Lake would indeed be useful, despite the workaround / local cache described above.

The reason I'm working on this issue is, in short: when a repository that depends on Mathlib is built on CI like GitHub Actions and caches .lake, a single cache ends up being 2-3GB, mostly due to Mathlib's influence.
Which means realistically you can only cache 5 or 6 builds' worth.

In our FFL/Foundation project, we've kept this down to around 100MB by using lake pack to cache things as a tarball, but I'm not sure whether this is a good workaround.
https://github.com/FormalizedFormalLogic/Foundation/blob/484e34cbcbdfb896f6161cbfd2c74788becff00a/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L37-L51

As a more concrete/practical issue, there's also the problem that, for example, in situations like a workshop where many people try out Lean all at once, downloading Mathlib places an intense load on the network.

There's already a proposal about making good use of tarballs, raised in the original comment thread of the issue.
https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/issues/10603#issuecomment-4379167728
This has annoyed me a bit in the past too. I'd probably also recommend testing out --filter=blob:none instead of using depth.

Personally, I frequently use git worktrees to run parallelized refactoring with multiple Claude agents, so having a small .lake is a significant advantage for me (for copying. currently I'm dealing with symbolic hardlink, but it sometimes breaks../), I'd like to seriously consider this. What do you think? @Mac Malone (reviewer)

@Mac Malone

I think you are the maintainer of Lake.
If you manage multiple projects that depend on Mathlib, the amount of storage they consume can become substantial. I believe that reducing this storage usage would provide significant value.

I’m not familiar with Lake’s internals, so I don’t know what the best solution would be. However, I think that even something as simple as experimentally adding an option to perform shallow clones could be a good first step toward incremental improvement.

@SnO2WMaN @Asei Inoue Thanks for looking into this! I have explored this area somewhat before and implemented a partial clone strategy in lean4#11662. Unfortunately, that PR was blocked on LSP changes, and I have not had the time to finish it. However, since the size issue seems to beocming more critical, I will see if I cannot extract just the partial clone from that PR and merge just that. I am not sure on the exact ETA, but I should have it done by at least the end of next week (assuming no unforesseen issues).
Sorry for the delay, but I have now implemented partial clones for Lake dependencies (and otherwised further optimized their checkouts). See lean4#14782.
